Analysis below drafted with an AI assistant, verified locally by me:

> as_strided is storage-relative; when its input is a lazy view of an unrealized
> producer, the stride enforcement in GraphLowering.run_node falls into
> require_strides -> copy_input and materializes the view's elements into a

issue.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

Here is the code to reproduce and it is found by our fuzzer.

```python
import os
os.environ["TORCHINDUCTOR_FORCE_DISABLE_CACHES"] = "1"
import torch
def fn(x):
    full = x.repeat((3, 2))
    return torch.as_strided(full[:, ::2], (3, 2), full.stride())
torch.manual_seed(0)
x = torch.randn(1, 1)
out1 = fn(x)
# print(out1)
out2 = torch.compile(fn)(x)
# print(out2)
torch.testing.assert_close(out1, out2, equal_nan=True)

```

The difference between eager and torch.compile is nondeterministic, but the assertion error always trigger like this:

```
AssertionError: Tensor-likes are not close!

Mismatched elements: 3 / 6 (50.0%)
Greatest absolute difference: 1.5409960746765137 at index (1, 1) (up to 1e-05 allowed)
Greatest relative difference: inf at index (1, 1) (up to 1.3e-06 allowed)
```

Analysis:

1. `repeat` is necessary to be placed in the compiled function.
2. when directly print `out2`, a runtime error is raised: `RuntimeError: setStorage: sizes [2], strides [1], storage offset 2, and itemsize 4 requiring a storage size of 16 are out of bounds for storage of size 12`

### Error logs

_No response_

### Versions

Versions of relevant libraries:
[pip3] No relevant packages
[conda] numpy                     2.1.3                    pypi_0    pypi
[conda] torch                     2.14.0                   pypi_0    pypi

issue.body:
## Issue

Fixes #197431

## Summary

`aten.as_strided` is storage-relative, but when its input is a lazy view over a
producer that has not been realized yet, the stride enforcement in
`GraphLowering.run_node` ends up in `ExternKernel.require_strides`, whose
zero-copy path needs a realized base. It falls back to `copy_input`, which
materializes the view's own elements into a smaller buffer and drops the aliased
storage and the storage offset, so the `as_strided` reinterprets a buffer that is
not the one eager would read: out-of-bounds reads (or the extent guard from
#192227 firing), and requests that stay inside the view can still return the
wrong elements.

This PR realizes the base before that stride enforcement when the consumer is an
as_strided-like op, so `require_strides` expresses the view as a
`ReinterpretView` over the realized base and keeps the storage and its storage
offset. Some storage has to exist for `as_strided` in any case; how much of it
gets materialized is a choice that is left to a follow-up, since a window copy
would also change observable aliasing.

## Test Plan

Four new cases in `test/inductor/test_torchinductor.py`: the reported repro, an
in-bounds variant, a non-zero storage offset, and an unbacked size. All four fail
without the fix.

```
python test/inductor/test_torchinductor.py -k as_strided   # 14 tests, OK
python test/inductor/test_torchinductor.py -k view         # 103 tests, OK
python test/inductor/test_torchinductor.py -k slice        # 33 tests, OK
python test/inductor/test_torchinductor.py -k split        # 28 tests, OK
python test/inductor/test_torchinductor.py -k expand       # 10 tests, OK
python test/inductor/test_torchinductor_codegen_dynamic_shapes.py -k as_strided  # OK
spin lint -- -m upstream/main                              # no lint issues
```

The auto-generated dynamic-shapes codegen variant of the repro is registered as
a CPU skip: the repro's shapes are static after `repeat()`, so that variant has
no dynamic loop variable to assert on.

## Checklist

- [x] Passes lint (`spin lint -- -m upstream/main`)
- [x] Added/updated tests (4 new cases in `test/inductor/test_torchinductor.py`,
      plus a CPU skip for the auto-generated dynamic-shapes variant of the repro)
- [ ] Updated documentation (if applicable) - n/a
- [ ] Included benchmark results (for PRs impacting perf) - not benchmarked; this
      can materialize the whole base instead of a smaller copy

## BC-breaking?

No. Only as_strided-like consumers of views over unrealized producers are
affected, and there the previous behavior was a miscompile.

AI assistance: the analysis and patch were drafted with an AI assistant; I
reviewed the code and ran the tests above myself.
